options: One qubit and one classical bit
Two qubits and no classical bits
One qubit and ten classical bits
A circuit with no qubits, used only for testing imports
questions.explain: The first argument is the number of qubits, the second is the number of classical bits — here, one of each. The classical bit is where the measurement result will be stored.

questions.q: What does the Hadamard gate (`qc.h(0)`) do to a qubit starting in state `|0⟩`?
options: Flips it deterministically to `|1⟩`
Leaves it unchanged in `|0⟩`
Puts it into an exact equal superposition, with P(0) = 0.5 and P(1) = 0.5
Measures it immediately and collapses it to a random classical bit
questions.explain: The Hadamard gate produces an exact equal superposition of `|0⟩` and `|1⟩`. The probabilities P(0)=0.5 and P(1)=0.5 are exact, not approximate, and follow directly from the gate's definition.

questions.q: What is the correct modern way to run this circuit on `AerSimulator`?
options: `qiskit.execute(qc, backend, shots=1024)`
`backend.run(transpile(qc, backend), shots=1024)`
`qc.execute(shots=1024)`
`AerSimulator.run_circuit(qc)`
questions.explain: `qiskit.execute()` has been removed from current Qiskit. The modern pattern is to transpile the circuit for the target backend, then call `.run()` directly on that backend.

questions.q: A real seeded 1024-shot run of this exact circuit produced `{'0': 494, '1': 530}` instead of a perfect `{'0': 512, '1': 512}`. What does this gap represent?
options: A bug in the Hadamard gate's implementation
Evidence that the qubit was not actually in superposition
Ordinary statistical shot noise — a finite sample practically never lands on a perfectly even split even when the exact underlying probability is 50/50
Proof that AerSimulator produced an invalid result
questions.explain: The ideal probability is exactly 0.5/0.5, but any single run only draws a finite sample (1024 shots) from that distribution. A split like 494/530 is a normal, expected outcome of that sampling process, not an error.

questions.q: If you re-ran the exact same circuit and code again with a different random seed, what would you expect?
options: The exact same counts every time, since the circuit is deterministic
A slightly different split of counts (e.g. close to but not exactly 512/512 again), since each run is an independent finite sample from the same 50/50 probability
All 1024 shots landing on the same outcome
An error, since AerSimulator cannot be run twice with different seeds
questions.explain: Each run draws a fresh, independent sample of 1024 shots from the same exact 50/50 distribution, so different runs naturally produce different (but similarly close-to-even) splits — that's expected shot noise, not inconsistency in the circuit.
